analysis: All four units are documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (MiMo/Flint/Flash-Next/Bonsai sections at head lines 2033-2639, plus other hunks outside the supplied units) and docs/developer/test.md (date bump, GLM5Next logprobs and OpenRouter test descriptions). No executable code, config, key handling, wire protocol, or authorization logic is changed, so no concrete security regression is visible. The inference.md excerpt describes existing contracts that are consistent with the threat model. Native MiMo media is noncacheable and target-only, with no media-prefix reuse, which is consistent with T-041's scope. Prefix reuse is described as using the exact encrypted store. The text states that restoring original tool schemas grants no tool, media, or memory-admission bypass. Bridge admission and context-limit checks are described with overflow-safe arithmetic. The patch excerpt for inference.md also notes a GLM behavior change in docs: variable-frame-rate video is now indexed using the track's nominalFrameRate instead of being refused. That code change is outside the supplied units, so the docs cannot confirm that decoded-byte, frame and visual-token caps still bound it. The test.md additions say logprobs rows are not drafted and JSON/forced-tool GLM requests carry no token constraint or logprobs. These are test-description claims only. Remaining integration question for any pass that sees the code: whether the GLM VFR-video change and the GLM logprobs-capture path keep the memory-admission and decoded-byte caps (TB-007) and the relay encryption (T-008) intact. Neither can be verified from these docs-only units. The docs should not be read as evidence that those controls hold.
